# Malicious Cron Abuse and Data Exfiltration(simulation) Attack

## Overview
This script was made to simulate a cron based attack inside of our Linux environment, including a payload script to simulate local data exfiltration

# Files Used
 'attack_cron.sh' - My main script that is used to setup the attack
'lab_exfil.sh' (generated by main script) - My payload script that is used to collect data
'lab_exfil_job' (generated by main script) My cron job config file

# Required Materials/Resources
- Linux-based host system (we used Ubuntu)
- Root or sudo privileges
- Cron service has to be enabled and actively running

# Starting My Attack
- It is very easy to run my attack, since eveyrthing is handled by the attack_cron.sh script all that needs to be done is start our central server using the command sudo python3 collector.py.
After that you need to open the console for the Victim VM and create a normal cron job using the command sudo nano /etc/cron.d/normal_behavior and fill the nano file with a generic cron job like 10 * * * * * root echo "SUPP" to show the dtection and mitigation only works on malicious files.
Next you will begin the attack by running the command sudo python3 log_agent.py & sleep 20 && sudo bash attack_cron.sh
The above sleep command is very important, we want to start the logging and detection script in the background but have enough time to start up before running the attack or issues can arise.
Everything else is handled by the detection/logging and mitigation system!

# Cleaning up the Victim VM
- To clean up the victim VM after running the attack, you must run the command below before running again to avoid errors
sudo rm /etc/cron.d/lab_exfil_job
